one_liner: Research JavaScript JIT in D using lazy basic block versioning; per paper snippets it beats V8's old non-optimizing compiler, not Crankshaft.
what_it_does: Higgs is a standalone JavaScript VM for x86-64 POSIX systems, written in D: it gives you a REPL or runs .js files from its own shell ('higgs file1.js -- args'). It also ships an FFI library and helpers for stdio, console, CSV and drawing. It implements most of ES5 plus Map and Set, has no Node or browser APIs, does not implement 'with', and its eval cannot see local variables. It is not an embeddable engine and does not replace V8.
how_it_is_fast: Lazy basic block versioning (BBV): the JIT compiles each basic block only when it is first reached, and compiles a separate version for each combination of known value types flowing into it. Type tests proven by an earlier version are dropped (the --maxvers option caps versions per block, default 100). The DLS-style paper adds typed object shapes, where shapes record property types and function pointers, and shape propagation, which removes repeated shape checks in inline caches. The record's abstract snippet credits these with removing 48% of type tests and cutting execution time by 25% against Higgs with plain polymorphic inline caches.
when_to_use: Studying or teaching lazy basic block versioning and typed shapes in a small, readable JIT. The same author later applied the technique in YJIT for CRuby.

Reproducing or extending the Higgs papers: the 26-benchmark list (19 SunSpider plus 7 V8 Benchmark Suite programs) and its runner ship in source/, and --stats prints counters for type tests, shape tests, versions and code size.
Experiments on x86-64 Linux with a D toolchain where comparing a BBV JIT against interpreters or baseline compilers is the point, not production JavaScript.
when_not_to_use: Any production JavaScript: modern V8 (Ignition/Sparkplug/Maglev/TurboFan), SpiderMonkey or JavaScriptCore are far ahead. By the record's snippets, even 2015-era Crankshaft beat Higgs by 49% on average.
Code that needs ES2015+ syntax (let, arrow functions, classes, template strings, for-of), typed arrays, Node or browser APIs, the 'with' statement, or eval over local variables.
Non-x86-64 or non-POSIX targets: the JIT emits x86-64 only and the README requires a POSIX OS, so there is no AArch64 (Apple Silicon), Windows or 32-bit support.
Embedding in a C or C++ application: it is a D program with its own runtime and garbage collector, and has no documented embedding API.

Anything that needs fixes: development has stopped (17 open issues, including a parser null dereference reported in 2026 (#219), truncated JSON.stringify output (#192) and a SunSpider date-format test that does not run (#112)).

integration.form: standalone executable (built with make; 'make install' copies the binary to /usr/bin and its JS runtime files to /etc/higgs)
integration.dependencies: DMD D compiler, GNU make, GNU time (tests), Python 3 to regenerate object layouts, libdl; libx11-dev for the draw library and examples
integration.min_toolchain: DMD ('latest DMD recommended'; the release flags are -m64 -O -release -inline -boundscheck=off -dip25). The last build fix (PR #218, 2023) only addressed Python 3. No building with a current DMD was tested this session.
integration.platforms: x86-64 only, on POSIX (Linux; macOS and BSD with notes, open issue #103 on OS X test compatibility)
integration.thread_safety: not documented (single-threaded VM; no worker or threading API documented)

gotchas: Possible harness bias: source/benchmark.py takes Higgs's own --stats 'exec time (ms)', which excludes JIT compile time (reported separately as 'comp time') and VM startup. For any other --vm_cmd such as d8, which prints no such line, it falls back to wall-clock time, which includes startup and compilation. Whether the paper's V8 comparison used this path is unknown, because the paper could not be opened here.

benchmark.py is Python 2 only (print statements, csv over a file opened 'rb') even though the README asks for Python 3. It defaults to one run, and its geoMean skips zero values in the product but still divides by the full count.
The binary must run from the source directory, or after 'make install', to find its runtime JS files. Those runtime files are compiled at startup, so short scripts pay a noticeable start-up cost.
The licence is not declared at repository level: the Modified BSD (3-clause) text appears only in source file headers (e.g. source/main.d), and the header still points at github.com/maximecb/Higgs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Do not pick it to run JavaScript fast: Graal.js (beats Node.js V8 on Are We Fast Yet peak performance) and V8 itself are the live options. Pick Higgs only to study lazy BBV and typed shapes. YJIT (catalogued under language-interpreters) is the production descendant of the technique.
verified_claims_summary: Search snippets of arXiv 1507.02437 (the paper itself was not opened, and its venue is unconfirmed) say that on 26 SunSpider and V8-suite benchmarks, Higgs with typed shapes outperforms V8's non-optimizing full-codegen compiler (removed from V8 in 2017) on 25, with speedups of up to 682%, while V8's Crankshaft is 49% faster on average. Hardware, V8 version, flags and timing method are unknown.
status_note: Abandoned research VM: the only recent activity is a 2023 Python 3 build fix (PR #218). Its licence is BSD-3-Clause per the file headers, which makes it usable as a reference implementation of BBV, but not as a maintained engine.
